# Seniors of NJ

> The home for older adults in New Jersey. Independent, plain-English guides to New Jersey senior benefits (ANCHOR, Senior Freeze, Stay NJ, PAAD, LIHEAP), Medicare, caregiving, housing, things to do and ways to learn, work and meet people. Every guide cites official sources and shows the date it was last updated. Not a government agency.

## Benefits & Money

- [ANCHOR, Senior Freeze and Stay NJ: the complete 2026 guide](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/property-tax-relief-nj/): One form unlocks all three of New Jersey's property tax relief programs for seniors. Here is who qualifies, how much you could get, and how the PAS-1 works. The 2025 deadline was November 2, 2026.
- [PAAD, Senior Gold and Medicare help: how NJ seniors save](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/prescription-and-bill-help/): One New Jersey application can cut your prescription copays to $5, pay your Medicare premium and add $225 a year for utilities. Here is who qualifies in 2026.
- [Social Security's 3.6% raise for 2027: what it means in NJ](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/social-security-2027/): Checks grow in January, but Medicare, the earnings test and your claiming age all shape what you actually keep. Plus how New Jersey taxes retirement income.
- [Food and utility help for New Jersey seniors: where to start](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/food-and-utility-help/): SNAP, senior meals, farmers market benefits, heating aid and free weatherization can all ease a tight budget. Here is how each works and how to apply this season.
- [Benefits for older veterans in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/veterans-benefits-seniors-nj/): Tax breaks, VA pension with Aid and Attendance, veterans homes and burial benefits for older New Jersey veterans and surviving spouses.
- [How to find an elder law attorney in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/elder-law-attorney-nj/): What elder law attorneys do, when your family needs one, county bar referral numbers, free legal help for older adults, and the questions to ask before you hire.
- [Long-term care insurance in New Jersey: claims and appeals](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/long-term-care-insurance-nj/): How long-term care insurance works, when a policy starts paying, how to file a claim for a parent, what New Jersey's Long-Term Care Partnership does for Medicaid, how to appeal a denial and how to find a lost policy.
- [Medicare Savings Programs in NJ: QMB, SLMB and QI for 2026](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/medicare-savings-programs-nj/): New Jersey can pay your parent's $202.90 Medicare Part B premium, and with QMB most Medicare cost sharing too. Here are the 2026 income and asset limits, what each program covers, and how to apply through NJSave.
- [The $250 senior property tax deduction in NJ: who qualifies](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/senior-property-tax-deduction-nj/): Homeowners 65 and older, or disabled, with very low income can take $250 a year off their New Jersey property tax bill. Here is how the $10,000 income limit works, how to file Form PTD with your town, and the March 1 form that keeps it.
- [Social Security offices in NJ: appointments and online help](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/social-security-offices-nj/): How to find your Social Security office in New Jersey, make an appointment, skip the trip online, what to bring, and how to help a parent with forms and payees.
- [How to appeal a property tax assessment in NJ](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/property-tax-appeal-nj/): Deadlines, filing fees, the Chapter 123 ratio test, what evidence counts, and how a win can change Senior Freeze and Stay NJ. A plain guide for older homeowners and the families helping them.
- [How New Jersey taxes retirement income (2026)](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/nj-retirement-income-tax/): Social Security is not taxed here. Pensions, IRAs and 401(k)s are, but the retirement exclusion wipes out the tax for many households at 62 and older. Here is how each rule works.
- [Retirement planning in New Jersey: a practical checklist](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/retirement-planning-nj/): Social Security at 62 to 70, Medicare at 65, required withdrawals at 73, and New Jersey's property taxes in between. Here is the order of decisions and where to get free, unbiased help.
- [Retiring with a New Jersey state pension: PERS, TPAF and PFRS](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/nj-pension-retirement-pers-tpaf/): How to apply through MBOS, what your tier means, the nine PERS and TPAF payment options, keeping state retiree health coverage with Medicare, and the rules on going back to work.
- [Medigap plans in New Jersey: costs, enrollment and switching](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/medigap-plans-nj/): Which Medigap letters are sold in New Jersey, what they cost on the state's 2026 rate chart, how companies raise prices, and how to switch plans or add Part D without losing coverage.
- [Life insurance after 60 in NJ: final expense and lost policies](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/life-insurance-seniors-nj/): What older adults can buy, what to watch for in no-exam policies, and how families find a parent's lost policy and get it paid.
- [Homeowners and flood insurance for older NJ homeowners](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/homeowners-insurance-seniors-nj/): What a standard policy covers, why flood needs its own policy, the FAIR Plan as a last resort, and what to do when a parent's house sits empty.
- [Car insurance for older drivers in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/auto-insurance-seniors-nj/): What New Jersey requires in 2026, why Medicare changes your PIP choice, the defensive driving discount, and what to do with the policy when a parent stops driving.
- [How to find unclaimed money in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/unclaimed-property-nj/): Search New Jersey's unclaimed property list for free, claim money for yourself or a parent who died, and check the federal and insurance databases most families miss.
- [Power of attorney in New Jersey: how it works for a parent](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/power-of-attorney-nj/): What New Jersey law requires, what an agent can and cannot do, how to get a bank to accept it, and how to cancel one.
- [Managing a parent's money in New Jersey: a practical guide](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/managing-parents-money-nj/): Bill paying, joint accounts, trusted contacts, Social Security and VA payees, spotting exploitation and keeping records for Medicaid.
- [Paying for long-term care in New Jersey: a planning guide](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/paying-for-long-term-care-nj/): How families combine savings, insurance, veterans benefits, home equity and Medicaid, with the 2026 look-back, income and spousal rules that shape every plan.
- [SNAP (food stamps) for seniors in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/snap-food-stamps-seniors-nj/): Older adults get easier SNAP rules in New Jersey, and a $95 monthly minimum. Here is how the income test, the medical and housing deductions and the application work in 2026 to 2027.
- [Free legal help for seniors in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/free-legal-help-seniors-nj/): Every New Jersey county has free civil legal help for older adults with modest incomes. Here is who to call, what they handle and how to get help for a parent.
- [Medicare scams in New Jersey and how to report them](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/medicare-scams-nj/): Free braces, cheek swabs and calls about a new card are all after one thing, your parent's Medicare number. How to spot the fraud on a statement and who to call in NJ.
- [Banking safety for older parents in NJ: tools banks offer](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/banking-help-older-parents-nj/): Alerts, view-only access, trusted contacts and convenience signers can protect a parent's savings without taking control away. What to ask for and what to do after fraud.
- [Probate in New Jersey: how the Surrogate process works](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/probate-nj/): A step by step guide to probate at the county Surrogate's Court, from the ten day wait to the Notice of Probate, small estate affidavits, fees and the executor's duties.
- [New Jersey inheritance tax: who pays and how to get a waiver](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/nj-inheritance-tax/): Children and spouses owe nothing, but siblings, nieces and friends can pay 11% to 16%. Here are the classes, the rates, the exemptions and the L-8 and L-9 waiver forms.
- [Leaving New Jersey in retirement: taxes, domicile and benefits](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/leaving-nj-retirement/): What changes when an older adult moves out of New Jersey: how the state decides residency, the move year tax return, selling the house, and the senior benefits you give up.
- [The new $6,000 senior tax deduction at 65: a New Jersey guide](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/senior-tax-deduction-65/): People 65 and older can deduct an extra $6,000 on federal returns for 2025 through 2028, or $12,000 for a couple. Here is who qualifies, how the income phase out works and why it does not change New Jersey tax.
- [Social Security survivor benefits for NJ widows and widowers](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/social-security-survivor-benefits/): A widow or widower can collect 71.5% to 100% of a late spouse's Social Security, starting as early as 60. Here are the ages, remarriage rules, switching options and how to apply from New Jersey.
- [Social Security spousal benefits in NJ: the 50% rule explained](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/social-security-spousal-benefits/): A spouse can get up to half of a worker's full Social Security benefit, less if they start before full retirement age. Here is how the 50% rule, divorced spouse benefits and the end of the GPO work.
- [NJ veterans property tax deduction and 100% disabled exemption](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/veterans-property-tax-deduction-nj/): New Jersey veterans can take $250 a year off the property tax bill, and 100% disabled veterans can owe nothing on their home. Here is who qualifies, which form to file, how surviving spouses keep it and what to do if the town says no.
- [Utility shutoff protection in NJ: winter rules and payment help](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/utility-shutoff-protection-nj/): Who the Winter Termination Program covers, the rules every utility must follow before a shutoff, how a doctor's letter buys time, and where to find money for a past-due bill.
- [Help paying water and sewer bills in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/water-bill-help-nj/): There is no statewide water aid program right now. Here is what each water company offers, how town senior discounts work, the winter shutoff rules for water, and why an unpaid town bill can become a lien.
- [Probate in Essex County, NJ: the Surrogate's office](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/probate-essex-county-nj/): Where the Essex County Surrogate's Court is, what to bring, the posted fees, and what Essex executors and families handle after the appointment.
- [How to appeal property taxes in Essex County, NJ](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/property-tax-appeal-essex-county-nj/): The Essex County Board of Taxation's address, deadlines, filing rules and fees, plus the 2027 Chapter 123 ratio for all 22 Essex towns. For older homeowners and the families helping them.
- [Working after 60 in New Jersey: jobs, training and your rights](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/working-after-60-nj/): Part-time work, paid training through SCSEP or a second career can all make sense after 60. Here is where to find help in New Jersey and how a paycheck affects Social Security, Medicare and taxes.
- [ANCHOR in New Jersey: what seniors get and how to file](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/anchor-program-nj/): ANCHOR pays New Jersey homeowners up to $1,500 and senior renters $700. If you are 65 or older and own your home, you have to file the PAS-1 yourself. The 2025 deadline was November 2, 2026.
- [Senior Freeze in NJ: how the property tax reimbursement works](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/senior-freeze-nj/): Senior Freeze pays you back when your property taxes rise above your base year. Here are the 2025 rules, the income limits and how to keep your base year safe.
- [Stay NJ: how the senior property tax benefit works](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/stay-nj/): Stay NJ aims to cover half of a senior homeowner's property taxes, up to $6,500. Here is who qualifies for 2025, how the math works and when payments arrive.
- [PAAD in New Jersey: $5 and $7 prescriptions for seniors](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/paad-nj/): PAAD cuts prescription copays to $5 for generics and $7 for brand names. Here is who qualifies in 2026, how it works with Medicare Part D and how to apply.
- [Senior Gold in NJ: prescription help above the PAAD limit](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/senior-gold-nj/): Earn a little too much for PAAD? Senior Gold cuts what you pay for each prescription and caps your yearly costs. Here are the 2026 income ranges and how it works.
- [LIHEAP in New Jersey: help with heating and cooling bills](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/liheap-nj/): One application covers heating aid, monthly bill credits and medically necessary cooling. Here are the 2026 to 2027 income limits and how older adults can apply by mail.
- [Meals on Wheels in NJ: home-delivered meals by county](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/meals-on-wheels-nj/): If getting groceries or cooking has become hard, your county can deliver meals to adults 60 and older. Here is who qualifies, what it costs and who to call in each of New Jersey's 21 counties.
- [Free tax help for seniors in NJ: AARP Tax-Aide and VITA](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/free-tax-help-seniors-nj/): Trained volunteers prepare federal and New Jersey returns for free every winter. Here is who qualifies, how to find a site when they open and what to bring.

In New Jersey, Medicaid's MLTSS program can, at home, in assisted living or in a nursing home. Here are the 2026 limits, the five-year look-back and how to apply.

A practical wellness guide for New Jerseyans 60 and up.

Medigap mostly does not. Here is how to compare what is really available at your address, with free help from NJ SHIP.

Here is what they cost, where to play a shorter round and how to stay comfortable on the course.
- [Activities for homebound seniors in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/activities-for-homebound-seniors-nj/): Can't get out much? Books by mail, friendly callers, online classes, safe exercise and rides for the odd outing can keep life full. Here is what New Jersey offers.
- [Gift ideas for older parents and grandparents in NJ](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/gift-ideas-older-parents-nj/): Theater nights, museum memberships, park passes, lessons at home and gifts of time. Holiday ideas for 2026 that favor experiences over more things to store.
- [How to stay active and social through a New Jersey winter](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/winter-in-nj/): Indoor walking spots, the gym benefit hiding in your Medicare plan, warming centers and the real risks of shoveling. A practical plan for the cold months.
- [Home Happenings: lessons and activities that come to your living room](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/home-happenings/): A New Jersey company that sends checked local pros to older adults' homes to teach music, art, yoga, cooking, games, tech and more, starting in Essex and Passaic counties.
- [When a parent stops driving in NJ: rides, ID and staying connected](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/parent-stops-driving-nj/): Signs it may be time, how to start the talk, the non-driver ID, every county paratransit number, NJ Transit options and how to keep your mom or dad active and social without the car.
- [Writing a parent's life story: memoir and legacy projects in NJ](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/life-story-memoir-nj/): How memoir interviews work and what they typically cost, how to record your mom or dad yourself, free tools like the StoryCorps App, New Jersey library memoir programs and tips for a parent with memory loss.
- [Senior centers in Bergen County, NJ: locations, hours and programs](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/senior-centers-bergen-county-nj/): Bergen County runs ten free senior activity centers with a weekday lunch, and many towns run their own. Here is where they are, how lunch and rides work, and how to make the first visit easier.
- [Senior centers in Essex County, NJ: locations, hours and programs](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/senior-centers-essex-county-nj/): Essex County serves lunch at its Cafe in the Parks sites, and towns from Newark to Livingston run their own senior centers. Here is where to go, how lunch and rides work, and how to start.
- [Senior centers in Hudson County, NJ: locations, hours and programs](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/senior-centers-hudson-county-nj/): Nearly every Hudson County town runs its own senior program, and free TRANSCEND vans can get you there.
